Theme 031 · Light, optics & texture

Vector-Phosphor Oscilloscope

A black-glass scope face with a faint graticule: a single electron beam draws every word, number and trace as one glowing stroke that leaves a teal phosphor afterglow. Acme Pulse is the trigger that finally locks a jittering mess of signals into one stable, readable wave, and the anomaly is the moment the beam turns coral.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Graticule — 10×8 grid with tick-marked centre axes; the constant "instrument" frame across every scene.
  • Beam head — white-hot dot with a two-layer teal bloom; the one "pen" that draws everything.
  • Persistence trail — 3–5 stacked path clones at decaying opacity; the phosphor afterglow.
  • Measurement cursors — amber dashed ΔY / Δt lines that turn an anomaly into a readable number.
  • Bezel strip — knobs + lit hardware keys (Roll back / Acknowledge / Start free) as the UI layer.
  • Lissajous idle — XY-mode loop that fills any "waiting" moment and the end card.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Beam draw — stroke-dashoffset at constant linear speed (a beam never eases); one full-width sweep = 1 bar at 120 BPM (2 s).
  • Phosphor decay — trailing clones at 0.6 / 0.35 / 0.15 opacity, offset 40–80 ms; keeps every stroke alive between hits.
  • Trigger lock — 6 frames of horizontal jitter from a seeded table, then steps(1) snap to stable exactly on the 0:08 drop and on each proof hit.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A scope is literally a machine that watches a signal and catches the glitch, so "background monitoring" needs no explanation. Risk: thin glowing strokes smear under social compression; keep beams ≥ 3 px and text large.

Adapt to your product: Replace the conversion trace with your own key time series (latency, sync lag, queue depth) and put your primary action on the lit bezel key; the cursor readout becomes your alert copy.
